.²1 Distribution, separation into parts.
.²2 Dissolution or analysis of a compound.
.²3 Severalty, distinction.
.²4 Diffusion, extension; {#tasyEva vyAsamicCAmi jYAtuM te Bagavan yaTA#}
 <ls>Bhāg. 6. 4. 2</ls>.
.²5 Width, breadth.
.²6 The diameter of a circle.
.²7 A fault in pronunciation.
.²8 Arrangement, compilation.
.²9 An arranger, a compiler; {#dvEpAyano'smi vyAsAnAM kavInAM kAvya AtmavAn#}
 <ls>Bhāg. 11. 16. 28</ls>.
.²10 <ab>N.</ab> of a celebrated sage. [He was the son of the sage Parāśara by
 Satyavatī (born before her marriage with Śantanu <ab>q. v.</ab>); but he retired
 to the wilderness as soon as he was born, and there led the life of a
 hermit, practising the most rigid austerities until he was called by his
 mother Satyavatī to beget sons on the widows of her son Vicitravīrya.
 He was thus the father of Pāṇḍu and Dhṛtarāṣṭra and also of Vidura;
 <ab>qq. vv.</ab> He was at first called ‘Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana’ from his dark
 complexion and from his having been brought forth by Satyavatī on a Dvīpa
 or island; but he afterwards came to be called Vyāsa or ‘the {%arranger%}’,
 as he was supposed to have arranged the Vedas in their present form; {#vivyAsa#}
 {#vedAn yasmAt sa tasmAd vyAsa iti smftaH#}; <ab>cf.</ab> also {#jAtaH sa yamunAdvIpe#}
 {#dvEpAyana iti smftaH . vyasya vedAn samastAMSca vyAsatAmagamadviBuH ..#}
 <ls>Bm. 1. 214</ls>. He is believed to be the author of the great epic, the Mahābhārata,
 which he is said to have composed with Gaṇapati for his scribe. The eighteen
 Purāṇas, as also the Brahma-sūtras and several other works are also
 ascribed to him. He is one of the seven {%chirajeevins%} or deathless
 persons; <ab>cf.</ab> {#cirajIvin#}.].
.²11 A Brāhmaṇa who recites or expounds the Purāṇas in public.
the seat of the an expounder of the Purāṇas.
